title: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) Call for Whitepapers for Mission Development Zone (MDZ) Outgrant
description: 1. DESCRIPTION 1.1. Growth of the U.S. Domestic Space industry has resulted in a greater demand for use of real property at U.S. Space Force (USSF) Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) by private and commercial entities to conduct spaceport support, payload processing, hardware manufacturing, testing, logistics, and other space-related activities. Ensuring that United States operators can efficiently process space systems, conduct missions in space, launch, and reenter United States airspace is critical to economic growth, national security, and accomplishing Federal space objectives. 1.2. SLD 30 requests white paper responses from United States Commercial Providers as defined by 51 U.S.C. � 50101(7) engaged in space transportation, spaceport support, spacecraft manufacturing, payload processing, assembly, test, space logistics, or other space-related operations on the buildout of the Mission Development Zone (MDZ). Respondents will offer insights, perspectives, and approaches to obtain real property-use agreements to finance, design, construct, operate, and maintain spaceport infrastructure. Industry insights from whitepaper submissions may be utilized to drive future RFI / RFP announcements issued by SLD 30. Specifically, the MDZ infrastructure is intended to provide critical support services to the Department of War (DoW), commercial spaceflight, and other spaceport users at an undeveloped area located in the southern region of VSFB�s North Base area. Development and utilization of the MDZ will be in support of maximizing spaceport capability and assured access to space to achieve national security objectives. 1.3. Description of Premises is at Exhibit B. Please note that the MDZ is not a space launch complex (launch pad), but rather a flexible development zone dedicated to supporting the broader spaceport ecosystem. This includes, but is not limited to, payload processing, hazardous processing, spaceport logistics, commodity storage, launch and mission control, research and development, spacecraft integration, and administrative/engineering spaces. 1.4. The USSF is gathering market intelligence to determine the feasibility of a future real property outgrant under 10 U.S.C. � 2667 to a commercial space services provider, spaceport support provider, launch service provider (LSP), space infrastructure provider, or other space-related entity to construct spaceport-related support infrastructure. MDZ support infrastructure may include, but is not limited to, the following activities: processing, manufacturing, logistics, and administrative support activities. Data gathered from white paper responses will directly inform the Government in determining optimal MDZ utilization and potential infrastructure requirements to meet Government and industry launch requirements. 1.5. To support its ongoing spaceport capacity expansion, Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30) continuously evaluates opportunities and fields requests for new missions. Accordingly, SLD 30 provides discretionary site access and information to prospective partners at any time. Spaceport users and providers responding to this call for whitepapers wishing to view the site may request a property viewing. Please note that scheduling a site visit does not constitute grounds for extending the submittal deadline. 2. CONDITIONS 2.1. This call for whitepapers is not governed by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and is not a Request for Information (RFI), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ), nor a solicitation announcement. Content of whitepapers will provide industry insight to assist the Government in scoping, planning, and defining requirements for the proposed MDZ. Content of the whitepapers may assist the Government in generating future contract requirements. Submitters agree and allow the USSF to use the information in the submissions for this purpose. 2.2. This call for whitepapers is issued solely for informational and planning purposes, and the Government is under no obligation to allocate property. The information contained herein is current as of the publication date but subject to change; it is not binding and may be amended in the future. While SLD 30 intends to review submissions, it is under no obligation to do so and reserves the right to cancel or amend the call for whitepapers at its sole discretion. 2.3. No funds are available to fund the whitepaper requested and the Government will not pay or reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. 2.4. Any future facility where energetic propellants, hazardous materials, and/or ordnance will be used, processed, or stored will require the development of an explosives site plan. To assist the Government in layout and zoning analysis, respondents should outline any anticipated explosive safety arcs, quantity-distance (QD) requirements, or specialized hazard mitigation constraints. 3. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS To assist the U.S. Space Force in scoping and planning for the Mission Development Zone (MDZ), respondents are requested to provide a whitepaper that addresses the following areas. The goal is to gather information on industry needs, operational concepts, and technical requirements to shape the future development of the MDZ. 3.1. Spaceport, Support, and Related Infrastructure Capability. To meet future U.S. Government and commercial space requirements, the USSF seeks to establish robust spaceport support and related infrastructure at VSFB. The MDZ, positioned in the southern area of North VSFB, has been assessed as a potentially viable location for development of infrastructure required for the preparation, operation, and support of launch programs, spacecraft assembly, payload processing, space logistics, and other supporting commercial or industrial activities that enable the spaceport ecosystem. The Government is seeking insights from industry regarding the MDZ layout and planned utilization including types of facilities that would be most beneficial to launch providers in this location. Respondents should provide an assessment with respect to the compatibility of the property with proposed concept of operations. To assist the Government in understanding this capability, respondents should provide a list of all desired facility developments intended to be constructed at the MDZ. 3.2. Payload Processing and Hardware Requirements. A primary objective of the MDZ development is to address current installation capacity constraints regarding payload processing. If a respondent�s concept of operations involves payload or hardware processing, the Government requests specific information regarding requirements to process modern 5-meter-class payloads and next-generation fairings. Respondents should describe necessary facility specifications to include cleanroom class ratings (e.g., ISO 7, ISO 8), overhead crane hook heights, clear span ceiling heights, and projected annual processing throughput. (Note: If a respondent�s proposed operations do not involve payload processing, this section may be omitted). 3.3. Benefit to the Spaceport Ecosystem. Respondents should describe how their proposed operations, facilities, or infrastructure developments will benefit the broader VSFB spaceport ecosystem, the commercial space industry, and U.S. Space Force national security objectives. 3.4. Parcel Selection, Layout Preferences, & Utility Requirements. The MDZ contains roughly 2,100 acres divided into general parcel sizes. The MDZ is located within 5 miles of Vandenberg Airfield with some parcels in the aircraft arrival corridor which will limit building height. description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades and Data Center Construction project at the Gainesville VA Medical Center located at 1601 Southwest Archer Road, Gainesville, FL 32608. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The scope of this project is to replace all data infrastructure across the Gainesville VAMC and to build a new data center to support that upgraded system. The data center building will be one story, and the footprint will be approximately 3,931 SF at the location of temporary trailer 11, which will be demolished as part of this project. The primary space within the building is the 1,177 SF Data Center Room. Supporting spaces include Unpacking/Packing/Staging, Entrance Room, and Storage. Mechanical, Electrical, and HVAC spaces. Additionally, a new generator will be housed in a separate Generator Room. Also, this project will be removing all existing equipment and cabling affiliated with the telecom rooms in all campus buildings. There are 59 telecom rooms that may require architectural work. Some rooms are existing TRs being reused, but most are new rooms being redesigned for the telecom equipment. In rare cases telecom enclosures are recommended and/or exceptions will be required. The entire campus will be occupied while work occurs. Contractor will have to coordinate room closures and shutdowns with the COR. Most rooms on campus will be affected. Some off-hour work is anticipated for more critical spaces. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in mid to late July 2026, with an estimated late September 2026 award. The period of performance is approximately 921 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000 (although the middle of this range is more relevant). description: Purpose: This is a Sources Sought. The Space Systems Command (SSC) located at Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is seeking information in the form of Statements of Capabilities (SOC) from interested parties in support of the SSC, Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power Directorate requirement for the Counter Communications System (CCS) Meadowlands as described below. The Government is conducting market research to inform its Acquisition Strategy. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources that can meet CFC/MD3�s requirement. The Government reserves the right to set this acquisition, or portions thereof, aside for small business � to include socially and economically disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, or woman-owned businesses. The Government is seeking contractors interested in and capable of providing all technical and logistical effort required to design, develop, and deliver capabilities to support the CCS Meadowlands system. Background and Description: Scope: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems. Period and Place of Performance: It is envisioned that the period of performance will be approximately 12 months in duration. The Government is working through the details to determine when the contract will start. The place of performance is flexible to allow contractor to provide an optimized solution. Background: CCS System: CCS is a ground-based counter satellite communications (SATCOM) system specifically designed to reversibly deny, disrupt, and degrade adversarial SATCOM. The basic CCS concept is to provide a flexible, modular, scalable, rapidly deployable system with a key set of signal processing/generation (SP) capabilities, selected counter SATCOM missions, and a robust transmit capability. Its architecture will be designed to host core capabilities and/or other more sophisticated �plug and play� type modules to address the ever-increasing number of technologies and assets available to our adversaries. The latest CCS Meadowlands will have upgraded capabilities compared to the existing CCS 10.2 Systems. The future CCS Meadowlands fleet will be composed of at least 32 systems. Meadowlands is a transportable SATCOM system composed of modular Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) / Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) Radio Frequency (RF) monitoring and generation equipment. The design incorporates multi-band antennas and equipment in transit cases. The frequency conversion system (FCS) that handles RF signals between the shelter transit cases to the antenna uses a proprietary photonics system. The system can be transported by C-130 or larger aircraft and by ground transport over improved or semi-improved roads. The system will be designed for operations by trained operators in US-controlled facilities world-wide, and in the Developmental Support Facility (DSF). The Meadowlands �Base Design� system meets current A-spec requirements. All systems have same Transit Case and Antenna configuration/capability. The Meadowlands base design system is comprised of the following major capabilities: Three independent, bidirectional antenna polarization paths Native Support for a single Large Multiband Antenna (LMA) Bands Supported: UHF, L, C, Ku, Ka Two separate independently controlled antenna polarization paths Simultaneous dual polarization operation Receive-only operation if desired Supports Base, and unique network specific missions Native Support for a single 1.2m Antenna Antenna Supports L-Band only The system can operate in three antenna Polarization Paths � Each Polarization Path Contains an Uplink & Downlink RF Interface. The system is capable of simultaneously operating/controlling up to three antennas and associated components utilizing three polarization paths. The Meadowlands system utilizes Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Ethernet, TCP & UDP/IP Standard interfaces for network communications (Data, Command, Control & Status) between Transit case assemblies, Antennas and the Software Server The Base System Configuration is composed of: 4 System Transit Cases in Shelter (Mission Control & Timing (MCT) Subsystem, Advanced Signal Processor (ASP) Subsystem, Shelter Photonics Unit (SPU1), SPU2) 1 Antenna Transit Case in Shelter for 1.2m Antenna (1.2m Transit Case) 1 Transit Case for Secure External Network Operations (Remote Ops Transit Case) � Contains Firewall & Encryption 2 Transit Cases outside by LMA antenna (Antenna Photonics Unit (APU)2 & APU2) APU Transit Cases The system can operate in the UHF, L, C, Ku, and KA RF Bands for Transmit and Receive via Frequency Conversion System (FCS) The production of the CCS Meadowlands units has been accomplished as part of a Pre-Planned Product Improvement effort. The program utilizes equipment from the CCS Block 10.2 systems as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) including the LMA Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, High Powered Amplifiers (HPAs), Dummy Loads); the 1.2m Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, HPAs, Dummy Loads), Power Distribution Units (PDUs) (in transit cases) and also external PDUs, Environmental Control Units (ECUs), Tent, and a Power Management Unit (PMU) Requirements: The market research obtained from this request for information will be used to support a Government decision on the award of additional CCS Meadowlands systems between seven and up to an additional 24 systems. The intent for any future systems to follow the same design and functionality as the existing Meadowlands systems for efficiency in sustainment, training and and maintenance for the operational units. Additional Background Information Please contact the PCO should additional background information be required. Should that Industry Day occur, contractors will be notified of the date and meeting details to allow for their attendance. title: Enterprise Management & Control (EM&C) System Integrator Requirement
description: The United States Government (USG), Space Systems Command (SSC), and Tactical SATCOM Division (SSC/TX), in coordination with the Directorate of Contracting (SSC/CGK), is conducting market research to identify industry partners capable of performing System Integrator (SI) functions or activities in support of the Enterprise Management & Control (EM&C) program. The USG intends to solicit and negotiate a contract or agreement with the contractor that provides the most technically acceptable solution to the USG under the current Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) on the Platform One Solutions Marketplace (P1SM). If interested in pursuing this opportunity, please submit a video to P1SM no later than end of October 2026 to allow time for your submission to be assessed in accordance with the competitive procedures of P1SM. The anticipated period of performance for the resultant award will consist of a 12?month base period and four 12?month option periods. The SI is responsible for planning, executing, and validating integrations between the EM&C platform and external programs/data repositories, including the Joint Management Tool (JMT), Unified Data Library (UDL), EMS Beskar, Blitzar, Protected and Tactical Systems (PATS) Mission Management System, and external commercial/government off-the-shelf software (COTS/GOTS). The SI contractor will not author core application code or dictate enterprise reference architecture. Core application code is developed by designated Development Contractors (DEV), while the architectural roadmap and governance are established by System Engineering & Integration Contractors (SE&I). The SI operates as the technical integrator and operational execution engine thereby, driving Program Increment (PI) planning, deployment automation, release orchestration, and enterprise-level test and evaluation (T&E). The SI must remain strictly independent of core software developers to eliminate any Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI).
